deliberate_simplifications: B1 only; q [1, Hq, L, D] float16 or float32; k and v [1, Hkv, N, D] float16 LOGICAL arrays. Row contiguity is NOT host-verified (row_contiguity_host_verified: false): the installed MLX exposes no public strides, so a sliced or transposed view is accepted as its logical dense value, and the native call passes ensure_row_contiguous=True, which may copy/materialize it. That conversion cost is outside kernel-only timing and must be measured separately. Explicit stride/offset/index/selection/ragged metadata keywords are refused.

D in {128, 256}; Hq % Hkv == 0; N % 64 == 0 (as upstream); N <= MAX_KV = 2147483584 so int32 uniforms and the causal round-up fit (MLX shapes are int32, so this is defence in depth); 1 <= L <= 4096; explicit Python float scale that stays finite, positive and normal after fp32 narrowing (the kernel, host mirror and reference all use the narrowed value); explicit bool causal; explicit int q_start with 0 <= q_start and q_start + L <= N
causal masked scores use the finite -FLT_MAX (MLX may compile with fast math, which assumes no infinities); every admitted query row sees at least key 0, so no admitted row is fully masked
fp32 output for numerical evidence; the returned dtype is always float32
no automatic dequantized full-KV path, no quantized tuples, no sparse/indexed selections, no masks/bias/softcap/sinks: all refused

key-set identity is a CALLER contract: shape and dtype cannot prove that k/v hold the complete dense logical keys; a pre-gathered sparse/indexed subset (e.g. Flash-Next QSA) must never be passed. No value validation: large or non-finite q/k/v and half-scaled query overflow need the native finite gate.

kernel_modifications_stage15: Race repair: ggml's single threadgroup flag sf[0] is written by lane 0 of every simdgroup (concurrent writers of the same value). Replaced by sgf[NSG]: each simdgroup ORs its rows' rescale decisions in registers (uniform after simd_max) and lane 0 writes only its own slot once per key block after the row loop; all threads read the NSG slots after the barrier. Lazy per-row rescale semantics are unchanged (rows that did not rescale carry sr == 1). Flag storage grows from4 to32 raw bytes; aligned total grows by16 bytes (D128 20640 B, D256 28832 B). This removes the source-level race; it does not validate native concurrency.

Launch registry: token-keyed weak records (flag weakref, expected threadgroups, id hint) removed together by the weakref callback; id hints checked by identity; claim-once under an RLock; GPU readback after the lock; CPU/non-array refusal before the registry is touched; kernel construction under a lock. A substituted factory outside the module's cached-kernel identity does not register. CPU lifetime tests deliberately substitute the cached identity to register synthetic flags, but never confirm native engagement. This is instrumentation identity checking, not protection against arbitrary monkeypatching.
